releaseNotes:
Release v0.23.2

New Features:
- Start the Succession background service at login without opening the editor, controlled from Settings (PS-282).
- Automatically deploy opted-in solutions when the service starts, with retries, logs and tray status for startup failures (PS-282).
- Manage solution Tools and Executables separately, with explorer icons for tools, executables and solutions deployed at service start, and matching MCP tools (PS-282).

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent duplicate service starts and improve messages for occupied ports, unreadable settings, keychain failures and refused login registration (PS-282).
- Harden DCC bridge authentication, command signing and Python value handling; refresh the bundled integration plugins (PS-281).
- Strengthen filesystem access checks, safe temporary files and atomic saves, archive extraction, asset references and network-path handling (PS-281).
- Harden HTTP requests, webhook defaults, backend identity verification, session-token handling, secret redaction and custom Python node approvals (PS-281).

Improvements:
- Bundle the code editor locally and prevent remote image loading in assistant chat (PS-281).
- Refresh Rust and frontend dependencies and migrate date/time handling to Jiff, with documented scheduling and Time Math behavior (PS-281).
- Make script-node input available through the SUCCESSION_INPUT_0 environment variable (PS-281).

Upgrade Notes:
- Deploy Solution now deploys only graphs in the Executables list. Existing tools remain tools; use Add to Executables for graphs that Deploy Solution should run (PS-282).
- Automatic deployment at service start is opt-in per computer and supports local drives only. Manually deploying a solution still supports network drives (PS-282).
- Reinstall the bundled DCC integration plugins to use the updated authentication behavior (PS-281).
- Webhook triggers now default to loopback and reject browser requests. Review the bind address of workflows that need remote webhook access (PS-281).
